convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I have been lying about my age — I'm younger than I look."
They light up a little when they see you.
"I needed someone to know — just one person. Thank you for being that person."
"What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing."
"Take your time."
"Still on that question."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"Good question." "Deborah owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I taste the water before the others drink. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Alfredo grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Alfredo is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Do you ever just need to be alone? Like, really alone?"
"I get it. Solitude's a resource too. Scarcer than food, some days."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on needing to be alone. One step at a time."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"See you around."
"What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones. ...sorry, I'm spiraling."
"Still on what you did for fun."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Anyway — I should get going."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Take care out there."
«Ẹ káàárọ̀! Ìwọ... kí ni orúkọ rẹ?»
At the hollow the ground is torn up. Something was here, recently, and it wasn't careful. Omolara's hand finds your sleeve. You leave together, faster than you came.
«Bẹ́ẹ̀ ni, mo rò bẹ́ẹ̀.» They nod, holding your gaze a beat longer. "Okay?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«N kò ní gbàgbé oore yìí.» (you catch 'oore' — kindness, 'gbàgbé' — forget) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Alfredo sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Halfway to the cache spot, Alfredo freezes. Fresh tracks — big. "We go back now. Quietly." You do. The wild, reminding you.
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
"Still on what you did with your hands."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Deborah always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Alfredo is already 👁️ Scout — that promise is theirs.
"I'm picking up Deborah's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
You show them Pawpaw — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You take those walks that don't need to happen. Still breathing your own air?"
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"We went over this," Hassan says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"Still on that personal stuff."
You show them Common Plantain — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Alfredo nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never did finish talking about what they confided — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'Can I tell you something? I have been lying about my age — I'm younger than I look.'"
They settle in like someone glad you're here.
"My wound needs a second pair of hands. Could you take a look?"
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what they confided."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "It's got me as well. a hot angry fever, can barely keep water down. Half the fire's got it."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Hassan nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
You show them Wild Garlic — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said fun was just being around your people. Do we count? Are we trying?"
They nod. "Okay."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff."
A pause. When they speak again, it's about something else entirely.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Me? Okay." "Listen. I need you to hear this before you go back out there."
"You've seen what's out there. I'm just saying — the treeline at dusk. Don't."
"Good. I mean it — watch yourself out there."
"Alright. Catch you later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
They go still. "So it's not just me. Good. That's... good to know. Bad, but good."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on how you slept."
"I can't. Not today. Ask me when the work's done."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Tucson, Arizona. I thought if you believed me, you'd keep me close. Close is safe. I wasn't thinking about you at all — I'm sorry for that part."
The silence stretches a beat too long. They study their hands.
The air goes tight. Their eyes narrow, just slightly.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They nod, already turning away.
"About the creek water run — I hate to ask twice, but it's still open. Will you?"
"I checked the cistern three times hoping I misread it. 0 liters. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"You saw it too, right? Duel. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"See you around."

You walk to the trap line with Farid. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
«হ্যাঁ, তুমি ঠিক বলেছো।» They nod, holding your gaze a beat longer.
«সব ঠিক হয়ে যাবে।» (you catch 'ঠিক' — okay) They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed.
«এখানে থাকার জন্য ধন্যবাদ।» (you catch 'ধন্যবাদ' — thank you) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You hold still and let the sounds settle. «তোমার কাছে খাবার আছে? কিছু?» (you catch 'খাবার' — food)
Farid laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — ঠিক বলেছো।" They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the sickness I'm fighting — still need hands. Are you in?"
"The cut's gone hot and it's spreading — I can feel it moving. Clean it out, wrap it tight, please. Before it turns."
Stand beside them first — same side of the Haven door — then help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"We lost Manuel and Easton. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Common Plantain — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I do push-ups at dawn. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.

"This was good." They mean it.

Farid shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
«ভালো বলেছ। একদম ঠিক।» (Well said. Exactly right. — you're fairly sure) They nod back, a little quicker this time.
«এই উপকার আমি ভুলবো না।» (I won't forget this favor. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«তুমি সত্যিই ভালো মানুষ।» (You're truly a good person. — you're fairly sure) You point at yourself, then at them, then at the fire. Together. They get it.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «এখানে কোথায় ঘুমায়? নিরাপদ?» (Where do they sleep here? Safe? — you're fairly sure)
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About the creek water run — still need hands. Are you in?"
"I checked the cistern three times hoping I misread it. 1 liter. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."

"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"Have you felt it? Like the air before a storm, but — bigger. Something's on its way."
They nod. "Okay."
"Out there? I'd rather not die today, thanks."
You show them Common Plantain — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I clean up other people's messes quietly when I think about what it wants from us. It wants something. Everything wants something."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

d37: What Deborah kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d37: "Deborah's gone." Alfredo looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Deborah." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d37: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Sidney blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.

d37: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d37: 📖 LEARNED: Reading People (Level 1). Microexpressions leak truth. Watch the eyes, not the mouth. People tell you who they are.
d37: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Deep Read! You don't just read trust — you read intent. Know what they'll do next. (Your knowledge of Reading People amplifies your open_book.)
d37: 📖 LEARNED: Mediation (Level 1). Let each side talk without interruption. Repeat back what you heard. People de-escalate when heard.
d37: 📖 LEARNED: Soft Step (Level 1). Move through woods like weather. Less noise, fewer surprises.
d37: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
